lines: The Statue of Liberty's copper skin is only as thick as two pennies.
The Statue of Liberty's COPPER skin is only as thick as TWO PENNIES.
Hang on. Two pennies? On something that big?
Hang on. TWO PENNIES? On something that BIG?
So how does she survive the wind? The secret's hidden inside, built by a very famous name.
So how does she survive the WIND? The secret's HIDDEN inside, built by a very FAMOUS name.
First, the skin. Workers in Paris hammered three hundred copper sheets by hand.
First, the SKIN. Workers in PARIS hammered THREE HUNDRED copper sheets by HAND.
But a shell that thin would fold like a soda can. So inside, there's an iron skeleton.
But a shell that THIN would fold like a SODA CAN. So inside, there's an IRON SKELETON.
A tower in the middle, and over thirteen hundred iron bars reaching out to the skin.
A TOWER in the middle, and over THIRTEEN HUNDRED iron BARS reaching out to the skin.
So the skin's bolted onto the bars?
So the skin's BOLTED onto the bars?
Nope, that's the genius part. The bars sit in copper clips, so the skin can slide.
NOPE, that's the GENIUS part. The bars sit in copper CLIPS, so the skin can SLIDE.
Why would you want it loose?
Why would you want it LOOSE?
Heat and cold. Copper and iron grow by different amounts. Lock them together, and the skin tears.
HEAT and COLD. Copper and iron grow by DIFFERENT amounts. Lock them together, and the skin TEARS.
And in strong wind, she sways about three inches. She bends, so she doesn't break.
And in STRONG WIND, she SWAYS about 3 INCHES. She BENDS, so she doesn't BREAK.
That's brilliant. So who designed it?
That's BRILLIANT. So WHO designed it?
Gustave Eiffel. A few years later, he built the Eiffel Tower.
Gustave EIFFEL. A few years later, he built the EIFFEL TOWER.
No way! A little Eiffel Tower inside Lady Liberty?
No WAY! A little EIFFEL TOWER inside LADY LIBERTY?
Pretty much. Holding up a skin as thin as two pennies.
Pretty much. Holding up a skin as thin as TWO PENNIES.
Follow for a new wonder every day!
FOLLOW for a new wonder every day!
